title: Phased Uplift & Graduated Overage Smoothing Playbook for Enterprise Renewals
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: reduce churn risk at renewal while capturing incremental ARR by introducing a phased uplift model combined with graduated overage smoothing. The playbook prescribes configurable uplift bands, optional multi-year discounts, and an overage smoothing credit that averages excess usage over the prior 6 months to avoid sticker shock at contract true-up. Scope: enterprise renewals (>$250k ARR) and mid-market renewals with >20% YoY usage growth. Out of scope: ad-hoc pilot customers below $50k ARR. Key trade-offs considered: 1) Revenue timing vs. customer retention — smoothing delays recognition but lowers churn risk; 2) Complexity of billing vs. sales enablement — more bands means better precision but increases contract ops overhead; 3) Standardization vs. Negotiation — propose templated bands but allow sales exceptions with legal approval. Proposed mechanics: - Uplift bands: 0-10% growth -> 0% uplift; 11-30% -> 10% uplift; 31-60% -> 20% uplift; >60% -> 30% uplift, with an option to cap uplift at customer request (legal-approved cap). - Multi-year anchor discount: 6% off year 1 uplift for 2-year commit, 10% for 3-year commit. - Overage smoothing: calculate average monthly overage over last 6 months and apply a 50% smoothing credit at true-up; remaining overage billed as phased payments over next 3 months. - True-up timing: default annual true-up aligned to contract anniversary; option for semi-annual true-up for customers with high variance (>=40% month-to-month). - Sales play: include uplift calculator in quoting tool and required checklist item on security questionnaire for uplift thresholds. Deliverables: PRD, sample contract language, renewal playbook for AMs, sales calculator, GA dashboard to monitor churn/NRR impact.
